The test image shows a tomato stem split open lengthwise, revealing:
- Dead, dry, tan/brown fibrous pith inside
- Dark rounded structures (sclerotia?) visible inside the stem cavity
- Green exterior on left transitioning to dead brown tissue
- Dry rot pattern with hollow/fibrous internal tissue

Top candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (sclerotia inside hollow stem) and **Southern_Blight** (also produces sclerotia). Let me view one reference from each of 4 different classes.
Southern Blight shows external white mycelium at soil line - doesn't match. The test image shows internal stem with dark sclerotia-like structures. Let me view one more class before deciding.

This is the confirmation I needed. The Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference (Bugwood_16, image ID 5593852) shows sclerotia up close - small, dark/black irregular bodies with white interior when cut. The test image (ID 5593851) shows a split tomato stem containing these exact same sclerotia inside the hollow, fibrous pith. These are consecutive Bugwood images from the same source.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: split stem with dark sclerotia inside, tan/white fibrous dead pith, black plastic mulch background
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot: matches perfectly - sclerotia form inside hollow stems, pith destroyed
- Southern_Blight: ruled out - shows external white mycelium at soil line, not internal sclerotia
- Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers: ruled out - shows black external canker, not internal sclerotia
- Sclerotinia reference Bugwood_16 (ID 5593852) directly matches the sclerotia in test image (ID 5593851)
